What makes the clownfish so amazing?

With handsome white stripes on an orange body, the clownfish is a small sea fish also famous as an animated movie star. Where it lives is truly amazing.

This book brings together all sorts of stories about the clownfish, including clownfish facts, the clownfish and the anemone, and ocean symbiosis.

content.alt: Clownfish - Nature and science facts about the clownfish
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the clownfish

The most amazing thing about the clownfish is that it lives inside a sea anemone that has a stinging venom. Other fish get stung by the anemone's tentacles, but the clownfish doesn't get stung thanks to a special mucus covering its body, so it avoids predators inside. In return, the clownfish keeps the area around the anemone clean and shares food, forming a symbiotic relationship in which they help each other. It's a friend that shows nature's wisdom of "living together and helping each other."

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why doesn't the clownfish get stung by the anemone?
A. It's thanks to a special mucus covering its body. That's why it can stay safe even inside a venomous anemone.

Q. What is symbiosis?
A. It's living together while giving and receiving help. The clownfish and the anemone are a classic example.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. It's great to explain symbiosis with the relationship between honeybees and flowers, and to observe it inside an anemone at an aquarium.
